answers.note: Practical triage and whole-class feedback with a four-week impact check, but no evidence base cited and little on what leaders will look for in book scrutiny.
Grounded in the DfE 2016 marking review, with a clear stop list, explicit statement of what leaders will check, and a timed staff-involved pilot with impact measures.
Thorough, implementable plan with staff consultation, scrutiny changes and a ready staff message, though the claim that whole-class feedback works rests on assertion rather than cited evidence.
Well-timed revisit-teach-practise-apply session with a pure /sh/ model, fully decodable word list, dictation and a decodable caption to read.
Solid, engaging plan with decodable words and writing, but the sentence to read is only offered as a challenge for quicker children and it wrongly lists 'a' and 'in' as tricky words.
Clear 20-minute structure with sentences to read, but it uses 'wish' (w is untaught, as the answer itself notes) in both the reading list and the exit check.
Accurate, well-interleaved task with a drawn AD/AS item and a full key, but twelve questions including a diagram, extended choice question and self-marking is a stretch for 15 minutes.
Clearly labelled micro/macro mix with mark points and an AD/AS diagram question, but 24 marks including several 3-mark explanations in 12 minutes is unrealistic.
Accurate mix with a levelled mark scheme, but no diagram item is required and fourteen questions plus an evaluative paragraph and self-check will not fit in 15 minutes.
